outcome.Summary: Implemented words.TopK in words/words.go: it streams the reader in bounded 64KB chunks (1MB bufio buffer, so arbitrarily large input and very long lines work, and a dangling partial UTF-8 rune at a chunk boundary is carried over rather than mis-decoded), tokenizes words as maximal runs of Unicode letters/digits with internal apostrophes between letters kept (don't, o'clock) while leading/trailing apostrophes are dropped, case-folds with strings.ToLower, filters stop words case-insensitively, and returns the top k by count desc / word asc (byte order), an empty non-nil slice for k <= 0, and any read error from the reader together with the partial counts. Verified with a temporary in-package test suite (basic ranking, ties, k=0/negative, apostrophe edge cases, stop case-insensitivity, Unicode, chunk-boundary splitting, read-error propagation, 1.6MB single line) plus a ~300MB perf smoke (~5s, bounded memory); the temporary tests and perf harness were removed afterward, and `go test ./...` exits 0.
